title: Synthetic probing + circuit-breaker driven deployments for safer model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a deployment mechanism that combines synthetic traffic probes and a runtime circuit breaker to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts resilient to model regressions and capacity shocks. This ticket covers: 1) a synthetic probing subsystem that emits configurable probe requests (short, medium, long contexts) to new model variants during canaries; 2) a runtime circuit-breaker that trips based on probe and production-signal thresholds and routes traffic to fallback variants or regions; 3) capacity-prioritized failover policy for tiered customers that prevents noisy failovers from starving reserved pools; 4) observability and automation hooks to enable auto-rollback or automatic mitigation (e.g., scale-to-fallthrough).
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic probes can be scheduled per-deployment with payload templates and expected assertions
Circuit-breaker exposes metrics and a state machine (closed, open, half-open) and can be configured per-route
Automatic failover triggers when probe or production signals breach configured thresholds and respects tiered capacity rules
A/B and shadow traffic instrumentation include probe correlation IDs so we can distinguish probe vs user impact in dashboards
End-to-end tests (integration) simulate regional outage and show our routing falls back to configured region/variant following SLA rules
decisions: Use synthetic probes as the primary fast-fail signal rather than relying only on sparse production errors
Circuit-breaker thresholds default to conservative values (e.g., p95 latency +15%, error rate 0.5%) but are overrideable per-customer
Tiered capacity policy: reserved capacity (Dedicated) is never preempted by failover traffic for non-reserved customers; we use a priority queue for failover drains
For cross-region failover we prefer model-variant parity; if exact variant not available, route to most-compatible quantized/half-precision variant with automatic metadata tagging
tradeoffs: Synthetic probes increase request volume and marginal cost during rollouts but provide much faster detection of regressions
Conservative circuit-breaker defaults reduce false positives but may delay detection of subtle regressions affecting quality
Enforcing tiered capacity prioritization can increase latency for lower-tier customers during widespread outages
Providing automatic variant fallback reduces downtime but increases risk of semantic drift; mitigation via evaluation harness is required
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag rollout in runtime to enable probe emission for a subset of canaries (2 weeks).
2) Enable circuit-breaker state machine and expose admin controls in Console (canary-only initially).
3) Run closed beta with two customers on Dedicated and one hosted customer to validate tiered capacity behavior.
4) Gradual enforcement: monitor metrics for 2 full production cycles; if stable, flip defaults to enabled for all canaries.
5) Post-launch: add automated canary analysis job that recommends policy changes based on historical regressions.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe template parsing and assertion engine
Integration tests that run canary + probes against a synthetic model simulating token-timeouts and output corruption
Chaos test: simulate region network partition and verify our cross-region circuit-breaker reroutes only allowed traffic per tier
Load test: validate probe overhead at 10k canaries/day doesn't breach cost SLO
E2E dashboards to show probe vs production error breakdown and automatic rollback events in staging
metrics: p95 latency delta >= +15% on canary vs baseline -> mark probe as degraded
error rate increase >= 0.5 percentage points over baseline or absolute > 1% -> increment failure score
semantic regression score (eval harness) drop >= 2% relative -> immediate rollback candidate
circuit-breaker open for > 30s -> trigger automatic traffic steering to fallback variant/region
probe success rate < 98% across 5-minute window -> block promotion
